# N4

> N4 renders editable video projects with a native Rust engine. Signal Atlas is the copyable 2D template. Its master schedules shots, XML describes their artwork, and all media travel with the project.

Start from the spikes branch on an Apple Silicon Mac. Install the prerequisites in README.md and run `just host-native` from the checkout root. Copy `spikes/examples/signal-atlas` to a new project folder. Read the AGENTS.md in that copy. Give the film a subject, a short sequence of beats, and a few frames where the intended motion should be unmistakable.

A familiar production recipe is a good starting point. For a launch title, choreograph the emphasis across editable words. For a map explainer, reveal a route and carry its registration through a camera cut. Supply artwork, type, footage and audio you can use for the production.

Edit `project.proj` for cuts and placements. A row such as `[0,64) V1 survey` places `sequences/survey.xml` for frames 0 through 63. V2 carries overlays, A1 carries sound, and indentation introduces parent-relative time. In a sequence, paint order follows child order. Editable labels use `<text><copy>…</copy></text>` with an explicit font, size and width. An `<animate attributeName="stroke-end">` on a path reveals its stroke using local frame/value keys. Edit the shared detail to update every placement, or duplicate it under a new ID for a different take.

Set N4_BIN to the absolute path of spikes/engine/target/debug/n4 in the built checkout. From the project folder, run `"$N4_BIN" validate .`, then `"$N4_BIN" render . --frames 42,76,142 --out /tmp/n4-look-01`. Review the actual PNGs, including both sides of any cut you change. Export with `"$N4_BIN" export . --out /tmp/n4-cut-01.mp4`. Use a new output path for each review. No generator is required to render the template.
